title: Chemical and transcriptomic diversity do not correlate with ascending levels of social complexity in the insect order Blattodea

abstract: This paper examines cockroach (Blattodea) diversity, ecology, and evolutionary biology. Blattodea encompass cockroaches and termites, representing a major insect order with diverse ecological roles. We review current understanding of blattodean taxonomy, behavior, ecology, and the evolutionary transition from solitary cockroaches to eusocial termites.

methods.name: Seven Blattodea species spanning solitary cockroaches to OPT and ST termites
methods.description: Two cockroaches and five termite species of low (one-piece) and high (separate life type) social complexity were sampled from BAM Berlin lab colonies and populations.
methods.evidence: we restricted ourselves to two re- spective laboratory colonies per termite species and two respec- tive laboratory populations per cockroach species.

methods.name: Hexane extraction and GC-MS/MS profiling of cuticular hydrocarbons
methods.description: CHCs from single cockroaches or pools of three termite workers were analyzed by GC-MS/MS and quantified as relative proportions in MassHunter.
methods.evidence: Three microliters of the resuspended extract was then injected into a gas chromato- graph coupled with a tandem mass spectrometer (GC–MS/MS)

methods.name: UPGMA chemical dendrogram on Manhattan distances vs published phylogeny (Mantel test)
methods.description: A chemical dendrogram from Manhattan CHC distances was compared with the He et al. (2021) molecular phylogeny using Mantel tests with 9999 permutations.
methods.evidence: A Mantel test (Mantel, 1967), conducted with the R package “ade4” (Dray & Dufour, 2007), compared the mo- lecular distances based on the published Blattodea phylogeny with the average Manhattan CHC divergence.

methods.name: HMM-based counting of CHC biosynthesis gene transcripts in whole-body transcriptomes
methods.description: HMMs built from orthologs across 17 insect proteomes were searched against the seven species' proteomes with hmmsearch, then verified against Swiss-Prot.
methods.evidence: These HMMs were then used to search the proteomes of our seven focal Blattodea species using hmmsearch with a maximum e-­value of 1e−5.

methods.name: Poisson GLM and chi-square tests of transcript and compound counts
methods.description: A Poisson GLM compared transcript counts across social complexity levels, and a chi-square test compared transcript counts with CHC compound counts per species.
methods.evidence: We used a generalized linear model (GLM) with Poisson family distribution to compare the variation in transcript counts among the levels of social complexity in our tested species

key_findings: A total of 134 CHC compounds were identified across the representative termite and cockroach species.
No consistent pattern of CHC chemical complexity paralleled the levels of social complexity across the studied Blattodea species.
The chemical dendrogram did not reflect the molecular phylogeny; a Mantel test found no significant correlation between them.
Total CHC biosynthesis gene transcript counts did not correlate with the total number of CHC compounds detected per species.
Counts of CHC biosynthesis gene transcripts did not vary systematically by social complexity level.
key_findings_evidence: We identified 134 CHC compounds in total from our representa- tive termite and cockroach species (Table S1).
Overall, we did not find a consistent correlative pattern of CHC-­based chemical complexity paralleling the different levels of social complex- ity in our representative Blattodea species.
Unsurprisingly, a Mantel test found no signifi- cant correlation between the molecular and chemical phylogeny (r = 0.3971, p = .1291).
We also found no significant correlation comparing overall CHC biosynthesis gene transcript counts with the total number of CHC compounds detected in each species (χ2 – test, r = 0.12, p = .79;
counts did not vary systematically by social complexity level (χ2 = 1.11, df = 1, p = .29)
